questions.q: What did Buck's winning the bet make possible for John Thornton?
choices: Buying a big house and moving back to the Southland
Paying debts and searching the East for a lost mine
Buying a new team of dogs to carry the mail
Opening a saloon of his own in the middle of Dawson
questions.evidence: journey with his partners into the East after a fabled lost mine

questions.q: How did John Thornton find food on the long journey east?
choices: He carried months of flour and bacon on the sled
He hunted his dinner as he travelled each day
He traded gold dust for food at every camp he passed
He sent Hans and Pete back to Dawson for supplies
questions.evidence: he hunted his dinner in the course of the day's travel

questions.q: What did Thornton find in the wreckage of an old hunting lodge?
choices: A map that showed the way to the Lost Cabin
A sack of gold nuggets hidden under the floor
A long-barrelled flint-lock gun
A journal written by the man who built the lodge
questions.evidence: John Thornton found a long-barrelled flint-lock

questions.q: At the end of all their wandering, what did the partners find?
choices: The Lost Cabin, standing empty beside the old mine
A shallow placer in a valley full of gold
A trading post where they sold all of their furs
A Yeehat village that gave them food and shelter
questions.evidence: they found, not the Lost Cabin, but a shallow placer in a broad valley

questions.q: In Buck's visions of the hairy man by the fire, what feeling stood out most?
choices: Fear
Joy
Anger
Loneliness
questions.evidence: The salient thing of this other world seemed fear.

questions.q: "Irresistible impulses seized him." What is an "irresistible" impulse?
choices: A sudden urge too strong to fight against
A plan worked out carefully ahead of time
A small wish that is easy to forget
A command given by someone in charge
questions.evidence: Irresistible impulses seized him.

questions.q: What animal did Buck find making the long howl in the forest one night?
choices: A husky that had run away from a Yeehat camp
A long, lean timber wolf
A black bear fishing in the stream
Nig, who had wandered off from the camp
questions.evidence: a long, lean, timber wolf

questions.q: How did the timber wolf finally come to trust Buck?
choices: Buck brought it a rabbit he had caught
It saw that Buck meant no harm and sniffed noses with him
Buck beat it in a long fight and it gave up and lay down at his feet
It followed Buck back to Thornton's camp to be fed
questions.evidence: the wolf, finding that no harm was intended, finally sniffed noses with him

questions.q: "In the end Buck's pertinacity was rewarded." What does "pertinacity" mean?
choices: Speed and quickness in a chase
Fierceness when fighting
Refusing to give up; stubborn persistence
Cleverness in hiding from others
questions.evidence: Buck's pertinacity was rewarded

questions.q: Why did Buck turn back instead of running on with his wild brother?
choices: He grew tired and hungry after running so far
He was afraid of the other wolves ahead
He remembered John Thornton back at camp
He got lost and could not follow the trail
questions.evidence: Buck remembered John Thornton

questions.q: What did Buck do for two days and nights after returning from the wolf?
choices: He slept by the fire and would not eat
He never left camp or let Thornton out of his sight
He searched the woods day and night for his wild brother the wolf
He hauled meat and gold for the partners
questions.evidence: For two days and nights Buck never left camp

questions.q: Buck looked like a gigantic wolf. What features showed he was not quite a wolf?
choices: His short, stubby legs and the curly tail of a husky dog
Brown on his muzzle and a splash of white on his chest
His floppy ears and small head
His spotted coat and long, thin tail
questions.evidence: the splash of white hair that ran midmost down his chest

questions.q: Why was the great bull moose in such a savage temper?
choices: An arrow was stuck in his side
Wolves had chased him for days
He had lost his herd in a storm
Buck had hurt one of his calves
questions.evidence: protruded a feathered arrow-end, which accounted for his savageness

questions.q: Why did the young bulls finally stop coming back to help the old bull?
choices: Buck had driven them far away into the mountains
Winter pushed them on, and only one life was at stake
The old bull told them to leave by roaring at them
Hunters with rifles had frightened the herd away
questions.evidence: The life of only one member was demanded

questions.q: As Buck headed back to camp after the moose hunt, what warned him that something was wrong?
choices: He heard Thornton's rifle firing again and again
A new stir in the land and a fresh trail toward camp
Skeet ran out to meet him, barking for help
He saw thick smoke rising high above the valley
questions.evidence: he came upon a fresh trail that sent his neck hair rippling

questions.q: Who had attacked the camp while Buck was away?
choices: Black Burton and his friends from Circle City
A band of Yeehats
Wolves
Miners who wanted the partners' gold
questions.evidence: The Yeehats were dancing about the wreckage of the spruce-bough lodge

questions.q: Why did Buck, usually so cunning, lose his head and rush at the attackers?
choices: He was starving and smelled food cooking in the camp
Because of his great love for John Thornton
He wanted the gold
He thought the attackers were only playing a game
questions.evidence: it was because of his great love for John Thornton that he lost his head

questions.q: Why was Buck finally ready to obey the call when the wolf pack came?
choices: Thornton was dead, so the last tie to man was broken
He was afraid the wolves would attack him if he refused
He needed the pack to help him hunt the Yeehats
Hans and Pete had told him to go away from the camp
questions.evidence: The last tie was broken.

questions.q: After Buck held off the wolves, what happened when the gray wolf came forward?
choices: Buck chased it into the creek bed
Buck knew his wild brother and they touched noses
The gray wolf led the pack away from Buck
The gray wolf fought Buck to become leader
questions.evidence: Buck recognized the wild brother

questions.q: What happens to Buck by the end of the book?
choices: He returns to Judge Miller's place in California
He answers the call and runs with the wolf pack
He becomes a lead dog for the mail train once more
He stays alone by the pool and never leaves it
questions.evidence: he may be seen running at the head of the pack
